boundary: a stock node's acknowledgement frames, captured on the air and decrypted with our own code

provenance.method: Two probes were sent with want_ack set and the replies captured: one channel-encrypted direct message, and one PKI direct message. The node's responses were decrypted and decoded by tests/host_unit, not by any third-party tool.
provenance.why: WIRE_REFERENCE.md records PortNum ROUTING = 5 but has never recorded that message's structure, so acknowledgement GENERATION could not be implemented from verified facts. Rather than guess the layout, a stock node was asked for one.
provenance.note: Our two nodes only. Ambient third-party traffic seen during capture is excluded per docs/TESTING.md.
provenance.clean_room_note: Black-box: transmissions captured off the air and decoded with our own codec.

acknowledgement_shape.carrier: Data.request_id echoes the ORIGINAL packet's id. That is the whole matching key, and it needs nothing beyond fields this project had already verified.
acknowledgement_shape.payload: a Routing message, carried as Data.payload
acknowledgement_shape.routing_field_3: the status. 0 on success, non-zero on rejection.

observations.note: SUCCESS IS ENCODED EXPLICITLY AS FIELD 3 = 0, not omitted. proto3 normally drops a zero varint, so an acknowledgement generated from first principles would have carried an EMPTY payload and might not have been recognised. This is the single most useful thing this capture produced.

observations.case: channel-encrypted direct message to a node holding our public key, rejected
observations.note: A non-zero status. The enum NAME for 6 is not established here -- naming it needs the schema read as specification. Recorded as an observed value, not interpreted. The plausible cause is that the destination holds our public key and expects PKI for direct messages, but that is inference and is not claimed.

findings: The acknowledgement is returned CHANNEL-ENCRYPTED (channel byte 0x08) even when the message being acknowledged was PKI (channel byte 0x00). The reply does not inherit the request's encryption mode.

The positive acknowledgement itself sets want_ack, and was therefore retransmitted three times on the measured ~7 s ladder because this stack never acknowledges anything. The rejection did NOT set want_ack and was sent once. That asymmetry is observed, not explained.
hop_limit on both replies was 2 with hop_start 2, against the probe's 3.

consequence_for_our_implementation.matching: Match an incoming Data with portnum 5 on request_id against the pending queue. No knowledge of the Routing message is needed to match -- only to interpret status.
consequence_for_our_implementation.generation: Emit Data{portnum:5, request_id:<their id>} with payload Routing{field 3 = 0}, encoded EXPLICITLY as the two bytes 18 00, on the channel rather than PKI.
consequence_for_our_implementation.do_not_copy: Setting want_ack on our own acknowledgements would mean retransmitting them when nobody acks an ack, spending shared airtime for no delivery benefit. Observed upstream; deliberately not adopted.

outbound_validation.what: An acknowledgement built by code/protocol/delivery.rs was transmitted to a stock node and ACCEPTED: its retransmission ladder stopped.
outbound_validation.why_this_is_the_test_that_counts: docs/PLAN.md's position is that a decoder reading their traffic proves half of compatibility, and the half that fails in the field is the other one. Everything before this validated that we can READ an acknowledgement. This validates that we can WRITE one they accept.
outbound_validation.method: A stock node was driven to send a want_ack direct message to us. In the control trial we sent nothing. In the test trial we emitted an acknowledgement through the shipped delivery::acknowledgement path -- not a reimplementation in the test, which would have proved only that two of our own things agree -- and transmitted it 1.4 s after their first send. Same session, same nodes, same message type; the only variable was whether we acknowledged.
what_it_confirms: The measured ACK_PAYLOAD of 18 00 is right. Had it been the empty payload proto3 would generate, the ladder would have continued and the failure would have looked like a radio problem rather than an encoding one.
Matching on Data.request_id is correct from THEIR side too, not only ours.
Our deliberate deviation of NOT setting want_ack on our own acknowledgements does not affect acceptance. Upstream sets it; we do not, and they accept ours regardless.
outbound_validation.note: Our two nodes only. No third-party traffic recorded.
